```{r}
# 1. Identify all unique macroregions from the saved predictions
groups <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(nested_cv_results_national$fold_details, function(x) x$group))))
levels_all <- levels(factor(nested_cv_results_national$fold_details[[1]]$y_true))

# 2. Reconstruct the fold_group_metrics table manually
manual_fold_group_metrics <- do.call(rbind, lapply(nested_cv_results_national$fold_details, function(fr) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(groups, function(g) {
    idx <- fr$group == g
    if (sum(idx) > 0) {
      cm <- weighted_class_metrics(fr$y_true[idx], fr$y_pred[idx], fr$w[idx], levels_all)
      data.frame(fold = fr$fold, group = g, macro_f1 = mean(cm$f1), n = sum(idx))
    } else {
      NULL
    }
  }))
}))

# 3. Now use this manually constructed table for your comparison
national_all_folds <- manual_fold_group_metrics[, c("fold", "group", "macro_f1")]
colnames(national_all_folds) <- c("fold", "macroregion", "national_f1")

# 4. Proceed with merging the regional results
regional_all_folds <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(regional_results), function(reg) {
  data.frame(
    macroregion = reg,
    fold        = 1:10,
    regional_f1 = regional_results[[reg]]$per_fold
  )
}))

full_fold_comparison <- merge(national_all_folds, regional_all_folds, by = c("macroregion", "fold"))
full_fold_comparison$f1_improvement <- full_fold_comparison$regional_f1 - full_fold_comparison$national_f1

print(full_fold_comparison)
```

```{r}
regional_win_summary <- full_fold_comparison %>%
  group_by(macroregion) %>%
  summarize(
    regional_wins = sum(f1_improvement > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    national_wins = sum(f1_improvement < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    ties          = sum(f1_improvement == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    win_rate_pct  = (sum(f1_improvement > 0, na.rm = TRUE) / n()) * 100
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(regional_wins))

print(regional_win_summary)
```

```{r}
categorical_vars <- regression_variables[
  sapply(national_df, function(x) is.character(x) || is.factor(x))
]
first_var <- regression_variables[1]

reference_levels <- sapply(categorical_vars, function(v) {
  lv <- levels(factor(national_df[[v]]))
  present_dummies <- all_vars[startsWith(all_vars, v)]
  present_levels  <- sub(paste0("^", v), "", present_dummies)
  dropped <- setdiff(lv, present_levels)
  
  if (v == first_var) {
    "none -- fully dummy-encoded (first variable, -1 formula)"
  } else {
    dropped
  }
})

reference_levels
```

### Post-LASSO

```{r}
post_lasso_national <- readRDS("../post_lasso_national.rds")
```

```{r}
# Extract the raw summary object
mod_sum <- summary(post_lasso_national)

# Search for the matrix
if ("coeftable" %in% names(mod_sum)) {
  raw_matrix <- mod_sum$coeftable
} else if ("coefficients" %in% names(mod_sum)) {
  raw_matrix <- mod_sum$coefficients
} else if ("coef3" %in% names(mod_sum)) {
  raw_matrix <- mod_sum$coef3
} else {
  raw_matrix <- as.matrix(mod_sum)
}

# Get categorie
category_order <- colnames(post_lasso_national$fit@fitted.values)
estimated_levels <- category_order[-1]  # drop the reference category (position 1)

clean_df <- data.frame(
  Term = rownames(raw_matrix),
  Estimate_B = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 1]),
  Std_Error = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 2]),
  Wald_z = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 3]),
  Sig = as.numeric(raw_matrix[, 4]),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Clean the text, Map Categories, and calculate Odds Ratio
clean_df$Variable <- sub(":.*", "", clean_df$Term)
clean_df$Eq_Index <- as.numeric(sub(".*:", "", clean_df$Term))
clean_df$Equation <- estimated_levels[clean_df$Eq_Index]
clean_df$Exp_B <- exp(clean_df$Estimate_B)

# Order the columns exactly as needed
final_data <- clean_df[, c("Equation", "Variable", "Estimate_B", "Std_Error", "Wald_z", "Sig", "Exp_B")]

# Render table
final_table <- final_data %>%
  group_by(Equation) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    Variable = "Variável",
    Estimate_B = "Coef. estimado",
    Std_Error = "Erro padrão",
    Wald_z = "Wald",
    Sig = "Sig.",
    Exp_B = "Exp(B)"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(Estimate_B, Std_Error, Wald_z, Sig, Exp_B),
    decimals = 3
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = Sig, rows = Sig < 0.05)
  ) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**TABLE 4**"),
    subtitle = "Modelo logit multinomial"
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    row_group.font.weight = "bold",
    row_group.background.color = "#f0f0f0",
    table.border.top.color = "black",
    table.border.bottom.color = "black",
    table_body.hlines.color = "lightgray"
  )

final_table
```

#### Gráficos curva de probabilidade

```{r}
# 1. Extrair o dataframe raw do objeto survey
df <- pnadc$variables

# 2. Definir variáveis
continuous_vars <- c("household_size", "household_income", "household_income_pcapita", "education_years", "wealth_index", "head_dependency")
categorical_vars <- c("family_structure", "worker_status", "single_mom", "metropolitan_area", "macroregion", "race")

df[categorical_vars] <- lapply(df[categorical_vars], as.factor)

# --- DEFINIÇÃO MANUAL DO EIXO X ---
idade_min <- 18  # Substitua pelo valor inicial desejado
idade_max <- 90  # Substitua pelo valor final desejado

# 3. Criar o dataset sintético usando os limites manuais
age_seq <- seq(idade_min, idade_max, by = 1)
synthetic_data <- data.frame(age = age_seq)

# Fixar contínuas na média bruta
for (var in continuous_vars) {
  synthetic_data[[var]] <- mean(df[[var]], na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Aplicar o reescalonamento da renda para bater com o modelo treinado
synthetic_data$household_income <- synthetic_data$household_income / 1000
synthetic_data$household_income_pcapita <- synthetic_data$household_income_pcapita / 1000

# Fixar categóricas na categoria de referência
for (var in categorical_vars) {
  synthetic_data[[var]] <- levels(df[[var]])[1]
}

# 4. Gerar probabilidades
pred_probs <- predict(post_lasso_national, newdata = synthetic_data, type = "response")

# 5. Combinar e formatar para o ggplot2
plot_data <- cbind(Idade = synthetic_data$age, as.data.frame(pred_probs))
colnames(plot_data) <- c("Idade", levels(df$tenure_condition))

plot_data_long <- plot_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Idade,
    names_to = "Condicao",
    values_to = "Probabilidade"
  )

# 6. Plotar o gráfico com eixo X manual
age_curve_chart <- ggplot(plot_data_long, aes(x = Idade, y = Probabilidade, color = Condicao)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  # Aplica os limites e quebras manuais no Eixo X
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(idade_min, idade_max), 
    breaks = seq(idade_min, idade_max, by = 10) # Quebras a cada 10 anos
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "proprietario_formal" = "#3B7593",  
      "morador_informal"    = "#DE8529",  
      "inquilino_formal"    = "#80C5D1"   
    ),
    labels = c(
      "proprietario_formal" = "Proprietário formal",
      "morador_informal"    = "Morador informal",
      "inquilino_formal"    = "Inquilino formal"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25),
    labels = scales::label_number(decimal.mark = ",")
    ) +
  labs(
    x = "Idade",
    y = "Probabilidade",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

ggsave("../outputs/age_tenure_curves.png", age_curve_chart, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

print(age_curve_chart)
```

```{r}
# 1. Extrair o dataframe original
df <- pnadc$variables

# 2. Definir variáveis 
continuous_vars <- c("age", "household_size", "household_income", "household_income_pcapita", "education_years", "head_dependency")
categorical_vars <- c("family_structure", "worker_status", "single_mom", "metropolitan_area", "macroregion", "race")

# Assegurar que as categóricas sejam lidas como fatores
df[categorical_vars] <- lapply(df[categorical_vars], as.factor)

# --- DEFINIÇÃO MANUAL DO EIXO X (Índice de Riqueza) ---
# Substitua pelos limites numéricos desejados (ex: -2 a 8, dependendo da sua escala)
riqueza_min <- 0
riqueza_max <- 8

# 3. Criar a sequência do Índice de Riqueza
wealth_seq <- seq(riqueza_min, riqueza_max, length.out = 100)
synthetic_data <- data.frame(wealth_index = wealth_seq)

# Fixar variáveis contínuas na média amostral bruta
for (var in continuous_vars) {
  synthetic_data[[var]] <- mean(df[[var]], na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Aplicar o reescalonamento da renda para parear com a métrica do modelo treinado
synthetic_data$household_income <- synthetic_data$household_income / 1000
synthetic_data$household_income_pcapita <- synthetic_data$household_income_pcapita / 1000

# Fixar variáveis categóricas na categoria de referência (1º nível do fator)
for (var in categorical_vars) {
  synthetic_data[[var]] <- levels(df[[var]])[1]
}

# 4. Gerar as Probabilidades Previstas
pred_probs <- predict(post_lasso_national, newdata = synthetic_data, type = "response")

# 5. Combinar e formatar os dados para o ggplot2
plot_data <- cbind(Riqueza = synthetic_data$wealth_index, as.data.frame(pred_probs))
colnames(plot_data) <- c("Riqueza", levels(df$tenure_condition))

plot_data_long <- plot_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Riqueza,
    names_to = "Condicao",
    values_to = "Probabilidade"
  )

# 6. Plotar o Gráfico
wealth_curve_chart <- ggplot(plot_data_long, aes(x = Riqueza, y = Probabilidade, color = Condicao)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  # Aplica os limites e quebras manuais no Eixo X
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(riqueza_min, riqueza_max),
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 8) # Calcula automaticamente quebras limpas no intervalo escolhido
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1), 
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25),
    labels = scales::label_number(decimal.mark = ",")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "proprietario_formal" = "#3B7593",  
      "morador_informal"    = "#DE8529",  
      "inquilino_formal"    = "#80C5D1"   
    ),
    labels = c(
      "proprietario_formal" = "Proprietário formal",
      "morador_informal"    = "Morador informal",
      "inquilino_formal"    = "Inquilino formal"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Índice de Riqueza",
    y = "Probabilidade",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

print(wealth_curve_chart)

ggsave("../outputs/wealth_tenure_curves.png", wealth_curve_chart, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

#### Outros checks

```{r}
# Restrict to the two categories being contrasted (owner vs. reference renter)
subset_df <- pnadc$variables[
  pnadc$variables$tenure_condition %in% c("proprietario_formal", "inquilino_formal"), ]

# How much of wealth_index's variation is already explained by the
# OTHER significant predictors, within this specific comparison?
summary(lm(wealth_index ~ household_income_pcapita + education_years + age,
           data = subset_df, weights = weights(pnadc, "sampling")[
             pnadc$variables$tenure_condition %in% c("proprietario_formal", "inquilino_formal")]))
```

```{r}

# Compare mean of wealth across par of conditions

svyby(~wealth_index, ~tenure_condition, 
      subset(pnadc, tenure_condition %in% c("proprietario_formal", "inquilino_formal","morador_informal")),
      svymean, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
subset_df <- pnadc$variables[
  pnadc$variables$tenure_condition %in% c("proprietario_formal", "inquilino_formal"), ]
subset_w <- weights(pnadc, "sampling")[
  pnadc$variables$tenure_condition %in% c("proprietario_formal", "inquilino_formal")]

subset_w_norm <- subset_w / mean(subset_w)   # normalize, same principle as svy_vglm's internal step

print("just impact of wealth")
summary(glm(factor(tenure_condition) ~ wealth_index, data = subset_df,
            weights = subset_w_norm, family = quasibinomial))

print("impact of wealth and age")
summary(glm(factor(tenure_condition) ~ wealth_index + age, data = subset_df,
            weights = subset_w_norm, family = quasibinomial))

print("impact of wealth and age and income")
summary(glm(factor(tenure_condition) ~ wealth_index + age + household_income_pcapita,
            data = subset_df, weights = subset_w_norm, family = quasibinomial))

print("impact of wealth and age and education")
summary(glm(factor(tenure_condition) ~ wealth_index + age + household_income_pcapita + education_years,
            data = subset_df, weights = subset_w_norm, family = quasibinomial))
```

```{r}
svyby(~wealth_index, ~tenure_condition, pnadc, svymean, na.rm = TRUE)
svyby(~household_income_pcapita, ~tenure_condition, pnadc, svymean, na.rm = TRUE)
svyby(~education_years, ~tenure_condition, pnadc, svymean, na.rm = TRUE)

# Quantiles give a fuller picture than the mean alone -- worth checking
# whether formal renters cluster tightly around a specific wealth band
# or are actually quite spread out
svyby(~wealth_index, ~tenure_condition, pnadc, svyquantile,
      quantiles = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
```
